title: Improved UI error messages when the parameter must be a constant

timeline.author: GrayFox1

diff.patch:
@@ -80,7 +80,7 @@ fetch:
 ---
 mutable pattern:
   - do:
-      catch: /all arguments to \[grok\] must be constant but the \[1\] argument isn't/
+      catch: /The \[grok\] method is sad because it needs constant arguments to work properly. Please provide a constant to the \[1\] argument/
       search:
         index: http_logs
         body:

timeline.body:
Closes #68324.

Improved UI error messages when the parameter must be a constant. In order to propose a new message, i've looked into Elasticsearch UI errors Guidelines and then, did some research and analysed the UX Guidelines to write effective error messages.

This change improves usability, since a good error message has three parts: Problem identification, cause details if helpful, and a solution if possible. I would appreciate if someone could give me some feedback.

I suppose it's kinder, but I was really looking for something different. I'm not totally sure what - that's why I was vague in the issue. I think my concerns were more around things like "if there is a single argument this sentence sounds silly" and "maybe we should use ordinal numbers like `second` instead of `[2]`". I don't think being polite is really important here.

reply.body: Thanks for the feedback @nik9000! I had the concern to try to reduce the negative impact of the user error according to the Guidelines i mentioned above, but since this is not the priority, i've just updated the error messages to display ordinal numbers and to be more direct to the point.

timeline.body: Hi @stu-elastic, I've just updated the method that converts int to ordinal number and implemented the code my way. I believe there is no more copyright issues.

Hi @andrevpessanha, that code is still very similar to the code from stack overflow and this change does not provide any additional useful information. To close https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/68324 we'd want to have additional information such as the argument name or value.

Unfortunately we don't seem to be making progress towards merging. There are still review comments which are unaddressed after the comments highlighting them. We are not able to merge this pull request without those changes being addressed.

We really appreciate your interest in contributing to Elasticsearch and hope you make more contributions in the future, however in this case we have taken the decision to close this pull request.
